solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Person imbibed decorated cup he had, seated on high table?

indicators.note: something imbibed is taken inside, so the word for person goes within the other letters
decorated suggests the letters have been dressed up and rearranged into a new pattern

blocks.note: 'he had' contracts to HE'D, joined to cup
PER is the abbreviation for person, as in grammar

explanation.surface: Someone drinks from an ornate cup while sitting at the top table of a college dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: A high table is the raised top table in a college hall; the question mark admits it is just one fanciful example of sitting up aloft.
explanation.definitionFit: Upperched is a literary word for perched up aloft, as anyone sitting at a raised table might be.

clue.text: Power race, e.g. Fastnet?

blocks.note: P is the symbol for power
to hare is to race along

explanation.surface: A powerboat or yacht race such as the famous Fastnet off the Irish coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fastnet is best known as an ocean yacht race, but here it is the Fastnet Rock lighthouse that gives the race its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A phare is a lighthouse, and the Fastnet Rock off south-west Ireland carries a famous one.

clue.text: Stones (flat), not good for formal dance

indicators.note: not means the following abbreviation is left out of the word

blocks.note: paving is flat stones laid as a surface
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A dance floor of flat stones would be unsuitable for a formal ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Pavin is an old spelling of pavane, a stately processional court dance.

clue.text: Do leader stirred up, with chamber full again

indicators.note: something stirred up is mixed about, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters of both words together

explanation.surface: A party organiser gets riled while the gun is made ready again.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun that has been reloaded has its firing chamber filled with a cartridge once more.

clue.text: Sly circumventing rule in secret place

indicators.note: circumventing means going around, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: canny means shrewd or sly
R is an abbreviation for rule

explanation.surface: A sly person dodges the regulations by hiding away somewhere secret.
explanation.definitionFit: A cranny is a small hidden recess or nook, a place where things may be tucked away unseen.

clue.text: Landing place on this side when river ebbs

indicators.note: ebbs means flows away, so that letter drains out of the word

blocks.note: hither is an old word for on this side, nearer
R is the usual abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A boat comes ashore on the near bank at low tide.
explanation.definitionFit: A hithe (or hythe) is an old word for a small haven or landing place on a river.

clue.text: Minor scratch may not affect this part of spiderman

definitions.text: Minor scratch may not affect this

indicators.note: part of tells us the letters are a piece of the next word

blocks.note: found running inside this word

explanation.surface: A superhero shrugs off a graze that never gets below his outer skin.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a shallow scratch only breaks the outer layer and leaves the deeper skin untouched.
explanation.definitionFit: Derma is the true skin beneath the epidermis, which a superficial scratch would not reach.

clue.text: Poisonous gas: a little coming up interrupts function

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the word reads from bottom to top
to interrupt is to break into, so these letters sit inside the other word

blocks.note: a bit is a little
sine is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A short burst of toxic fumes disrupts a ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Stibine is antimony hydride, a highly toxic gas comparable to arsine.

clue.text: Girl pocketing key that's this and this!

definitions.text: Girl pocketing key that's this and this!

indicators.note: pocketing means putting away inside, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: a maid is a girl
a key or cay is a small island, abbreviated ISL

explanation.surface: A girl who has pocketed a key that has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The key is both lost in her pocket and lost inside the word, so the answer describes it twice over, hence 'this and this'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mislaid means put somewhere and then forgotten, as a key pocketed and lost would be.

clue.text: Gardenia Jim interspersed with peas held together by stick (11, two words)

indicators.note: interspersed means scattered among, so single letters are dropped between the others
held together by means clasped on both sides by the following word

blocks.note: a cane is a stick
taken as written
taken as written, letters to scatter

explanation.surface: Jim's garden has gardenias planted among the peas, tied to canes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interspersed' means Jim's three letters are scattered singly through the other word rather than kept together.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape jasmine is the common name of Gardenia jasminoides, a fragrant shrub.

clue.text: Hunk gargles boozily, common sight at Bierfest

indicators.note: something done boozily is done drunkenly and haphazardly, so the letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of both words together

explanation.surface: A burly man drinks clumsily at a German beer festival.
explanation.definitionFit: An enghalskrug is a narrow-necked German stoneware jug, the sort seen at a beer festival.

clue.text: Favourite about finished, reverse of ideal change of fortune

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word goes round the second
reverse of asks for the word read backwards

blocks.note: a pet is a favourite
ripe in the sense of fully developed, matured
A1 means first-rate or ideal, written here as AI

explanation.surface: A favourite is done for, a reversal of the ideal fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Peripetia is the sudden reversal of circumstances in a drama, a turn in a hero's fortune.

clue.text: Fleet in point of fact welcoming sign of victory

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in a guest, so one word holds the letter inside

blocks.note: nay used in the sense 'indeed, in fact'
V for victory, the famous hand sign

explanation.surface: A fleet returns home to be greeted with the V sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A navy is a nation's fleet of warships taken as a whole.

clue.text: Succinct drama is replaced by page

indicators.note: replaced by means one part of the word is swapped out for another

blocks.note: a crisis is a drama
taken as written, the part swapped out
P is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: A tightly written play cut down to a single page.
explanation.definitionFit: Crisp style is brief and to the point, a synonym of succinct.

clue.text: Carnivore like this appears in ring jumping around

indicators.note: jumping around suggests the letters leap into a new order
appears in means shows up inside the other word

blocks.note: taken as written
so means in this way

explanation.surface: A circus beast leaps about the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The grison is a South American weasel-like carnivorous mammal.

clue.text: Hornless stag, or cow?

blocks.note: first meaning: ... (or hummel), of a stag or cattle without horns
second meaning: to cow, abase or humiliate

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks whether a beast is a deer or a cow; really 'cow' is a verb, and 'stag' just shows what kind of creature the first sense describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists humble as a Scots-derived adjective for hornless animals, and the verb means to subdue or browbeat.

clue.text: When you see wife avoiding cooked bean, don't eat it!

definitions.text: When you see wife avoiding cooked bean, don't eat it!

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping clear of, so that letter is dropped
cooked means altered by preparation, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
W is the abbreviation for wife
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning against eating a dodgy bean dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and a warning: this plant is poisonous, so do not eat it.
explanation.definitionFit: Henbane is a poisonous plant of the nightshade family, so it should never be eaten.

clue.text: Notice I'll be brought in to direct with more consistency

indicators.note: brought in to means placed inside the following word

blocks.note: to steer is to direct
an ad is a notice
the I of I'll, standing as itself

explanation.surface: A director promising to bring more consistency to the production.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadier, the comparative of steady, means more regular or consistent.

clue.text: Former trust: a relationship is lacking in it

indicators.note: is lacking means the following letters are missing from the word

blocks.note: an affinity is a relationship or close connection
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned bond of trust in which there is no real relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: Affy is an obsolete word meaning to trust or confide, hence 'former'.

clue.text: What'll aid streamlining following publication?

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for following
an airing is a making public

explanation.surface: Editing that will streamline a text after it is published.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairing is a shaped casing fitted to a vehicle or aircraft to reduce drag, a streamlining part.

clue.text: She's a discerning foodie, and a friend in trouble

indicators.note: in trouble suggests disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters of both words together

explanation.surface: A gourmet woman who is also a friend going through a hard time.
explanation.definitionFit: A friande is a female gourmet, the feminine of friand, someone fond of delicacies.

clue.text: Muscular disorder not returning Daisy's got round after treatment

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word reads the other way
got round means surrounded, so the name wraps the other word
after treatment means altered by handling, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: the name, whose possessive 's means 'has'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Daisy's muscle complaint has gone away after a course of treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Dystonia is a neurological condition causing involuntary muscle contractions.

clue.text: Bass polished off, beer glass refreshed – sign of generous host?

indicators.note: polished off means finished off and gone, so that letter is removed
refreshed suggests made new, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for bass in music
the letters of both words together

explanation.surface: A host whose guests finish a Bass ale and get a refill straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: Bass is a famous brand of English ale, which helps the surface hide that it is the musical abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is liberal giving, which a host keeping glasses topped up displays.

clue.text: It smoulders in thurible, around start of communion say

indicators.note: start of means only the opening letter is used
around means surrounding, so one word wraps the letter

blocks.note: to state is to say
the first letter of communion

explanation.surface: Incense burns in a censer during a communion service.
explanation.definitionFit: Stacte is a sweet spice burned as incense in ancient worship, as in a thurible, a church censer.

clue.text: Large wine range available from hired salesman

indicators.note: available from means the letters can be taken out of the words that follow

blocks.note: found running across these words

explanation.surface: A rep hired to sell a big selection of wines.
explanation.definitionFit: Reds, red wines collectively, form a large category of the wines on any list.

clue.text: Party thrown, dukedom's ruined immediately (5, two words)

indicators.note: thrown means cast out, so those letters are removed
ruined means wrecked, so the letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: a do is a party
taken as written, with 's meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: A wild party wrecks a duke's estate at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing D and O from DUKEDOM leaves UKEDM to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Ek dum is Anglo-Indian slang, from Hindi, meaning at once or immediately.

clue.text: Miss out, having to accept tawdry stuff, in socialistic regime?

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of order
having to accept means taking in, so the other word goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
tat is cheap tawdry goods

explanation.surface: Missing out because one must put up with shoddy goods under a socialist government.
explanation.definitionFit: Statism is a political system with centralised state control of the economy, associated with socialism.

clue.text: What harvester grips and studies lifted round acreage

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means raised up, read from bottom to top
round means surrounding the next letter

blocks.note: dens are private studies
A is the abbreviation for acre or area

explanation.surface: A farmworker keeps a firm hold while studying fields of crops.
explanation.definitionFit: A snead (snath) is the shaft of a scythe, the handle a reaper holds.

clue.text: Like an anvil, more than half banged up?

definitions.note: describes the anvil-shaped ear bone, a noun

indicators.note: more than half means only most of the word is used, its end cut off

blocks.note: incuse means stamped or hammered in, as on a coin

explanation.surface: Something hammered on an anvil is more than half knocked about.
explanation.definitionFit: The incus is the anvil-shaped small bone of the middle ear, its name Latin for anvil.

clue.text: Some Finns are found in South America having run away

indicators.note: having something away means it is gone, so that letter is taken out
found in means located inside the other letters

blocks.note: S for south
Amer. is an abbreviation for America
R for run, as in cricket scores
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A

explanation.surface: Some Finns have emigrated to South America.
explanation.walkthrough: SAME is S plus AMER less its R; the A for are then goes inside after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saame (Sami or Lapps) are an indigenous people of northern Finland and Scandinavia.

clue.text: Nautical measure including trawl for supposed monster

indicators.note: including means taking in, so the measure wraps the other word

blocks.note: kn is the abbreviation for knot, a speed at sea
to rake is to search through, to trawl

explanation.surface: Sailors measure a catch hauled in while hunting a sea monster.
explanation.definitionFit: The kraken is a legendary giant sea creature said to haunt Norwegian waters.

clue.text: Lord, one accompanied by sweetheart, independent

blocks.note: a means one
dona (or donah) is old slang for a sweetheart
I is the abbreviation for independent

explanation.surface: A lord brings a girlfriend but remains his own man.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonai is a Hebrew title for God, translated 'my Lord' in scripture.

clue.text: Having crust that's dry, one assumes?

definitions.text: Having crust that's dry, one assumes?

blocks.note: surface reading: describing stale bread or a dried-out loaf
setter's reading: the adjective describes simply having an outer skin, which one presumes would be dry

explanation.walkthrough: The adjective literally means having a rind; the clue jokes that anything so described is presumably dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Rindy means having a rind or tough outer skin, as on cheese or fruit.

clue.text: Image showing centre of viscera, taken in hospital?

indicators.note: centre of means only the middle letter is taken
taken in means placed inside the next word

blocks.note: a san is a sanatorium, a kind of hospital, hence the question mark
the middle letter of viscera

explanation.surface: A medical image of someone's internal organs taken at hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A scan is an image of the body's interior produced by medical imaging.

clue.text: Usual trend left by river forming waves

indicators.note: left by means abandoned, so that letter departs
forming means shaping into something new, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of both words together
R for river

explanation.surface: A river's usual course flows away in ripples.
explanation.definitionFit: To undulate is to move with a wavelike motion, rising and falling.

clue.text: Graves when neglected may be so disordered and want backing

definitions.text: Graves when neglected may be so

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word reads in reverse

blocks.note: mad means mentally disordered
a want is a desire

explanation.surface: Neglected graves may become chaotic and in need of support.
explanation.walkthrough: Graves here is the white wine from Bordeaux, not burial places.
explanation.definitionFit: A maderised wine has oxidised and turned brownish like Madeira, as a badly kept Graves might.
